page.title: IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship
page.introduction: Porsche Penske Motorsport dominated the 2025 IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship with the advanced 963 and a skilled driver lineup. After winning back-to-back titles in 2024 and 2025, the team showcased resilience and strategy across top North American tracks, securing consistent top finishes and reinforcing Porsche’s excellence in motorsport.

accordion.title: Five things you need to know about IMSA

items.title: When did the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship start?
items.description: Sanctioning body IMSA was founded in 1969 and has run various iterations of America's top-level sportscar championship since then. In its current guise, the inaugural season took place in 2014, and was initially known as the United SportsCar Championship. The current championship’s first year included 13 rounds, beginning with the Rolex 24 at Daytona and culminating in Petit Le Mans at Road Atlanta. It rebranded to its current name for the 2016 season.

items.title: How many rounds are on the IMSA calendar?
items.description: The IMSA calendar consists of 11 rounds, including five races which form the Michelin Endurance Cup. There are two rounds which do not feature the top class, GTP, at Mosport and Virginia International Raceway. The season once again starts with the Daytona 24 Hours in January and ends at Road Atlanta for the iconic Petit Le Mans in October.

items.title: Which classes compete in the IMSA championship?
items.description: Like the World Endurance Championship, the IMSA SportsCar Championship features two types of cars – Prototype and GT. They are split into four classes: Grand Touring Prototype (GTP), Le Mans Prototype 2 (LMP2), GT Daytona Pro (GTD Pro) and GT Daytona (GTD). GTP cars are the fastest, and are designed for the track, while GT entries are based on production models. The GTP class uses rules similar to that of the World Endurance Championship, allowing cars to compete in both GTP and the WEC’s Hypercar category.

items.title: What does the Porsche IMSA program look like?
items.description: Porsche Penske Motorsport competes in the top tier of IMSA: The GTP class. There are two factory Porsche GTP entries, while JDC-Miller MotorSports also runs one Porsche 963. Across GTD Pro and GTD, there are four Porsche 911 GT3 R, run by Manthey Racing, AO Racing and Wright Motorsports.

items.title: How many wins does Porsche have in IMSA?
items.description: Porsche has over 600 wins in the IMSA SportsCar Championship, reaching that milestone with the #6 car’s GTP victory at Laguna Seca, while Team Penske clocked up its 100th sportscar win at the same race. The Porsche 963 took its first win - after just three races - at Long Beach in 2023 to begin a stellar run of results in its first two seasons in the championship.

moduleDriverList.title: Porsche IMSA driver line-up for 2026
moduleDriverList.description: The Porsche Penske Motorsport team is back with a new line-up ready to take on the circuits in the IMSA. Get to know the dedicated drivers and find out what sets them apart from their competition.

driversAndNumbers.title: Kévin Estre
driversAndNumbers.introduction: A Porsche driver since 2016, Estre was a key part of the 2018 Le Mans class-winning Porsche GT Team alongside Christensen and Vanthoor. In 2026 he is competing in the IMSA WeatherTec SportsCar Championship on the Porsche Penske Motorsport 963 #6.
driversAndNumbers.introColumn1: Endurance racing is all about the team. Estre believes putting ego to one side is key: “The whole group has to work, the harmony between all these people makes you win a race, and not your own performance on one lap.”
driversAndNumbers.introColumn2: He credits the team, which have already led to success, and believes “everybody has to be able to work together to create the results.”

driversAndNumbers.title: Laurens Vanthoor
driversAndNumbers.introduction: Laurens is known for his skill and consistency as a former WEC driver for Porsche Penske Motorsport. In 2026 he is piloting car #6 in the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship. He brings experience and speed to the team, as the team is aiming for top finishes and championship success in North America's endurance racing series.
driversAndNumbers.introColumn1: Vanthoor’s Porsche journey began in GT racing, but he says he had been “dreaming of this opportunity to drive in Hypercars for a long time.
driversAndNumbers.introColumn2: To be able to do that with Porsche is, I think, the best place you can be.” His sage advice to newcomers? "If you put in the effort and the work, things will come your way sooner or later.”

driversAndNumbers.title: Matt Campbell
driversAndNumbers.introduction: Having transitioned to compete as an endurance driver for Porsche Penske Motorsport in the 2026 IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship, Campbell brings his proven skill and experience to the team. A Porsche works driver since 2019 and winner of the 2024 24 Hours of Daytona, he continues to showcase his talent in endurance racing.
driversAndNumbers.introColumn1: From humble beginnings racing in one-make series in Australia to progressing through the junior ranks, Campbell had always dreamed of being a Porsche factory driver.
driversAndNumbers.introColumn2: He says it was "the last item to tick off in my journey of my career that I set out to try and achieve" - and it took just eight years from taking his first steps to reaching the very top of the Porsche motorsport pyramid.

driversAndNumbers.title: Felipe Nasr
driversAndNumbers.introduction: Brazilian driver Felipe Nasr raced in Formula 1, but since he left his big goal was to race for a manufacturer he could write his name in history with. He joined Porsche in 2022 to help develop the 963 LMDh prototype.
driversAndNumbers.introColumn1: Nasr has won plenty of races in his career, whether that’s in single-seaters or sportscars. But he says winning 24 Hours of Daytona for the first time in 2024 was unique.
driversAndNumbers.introColumn2: "All the other championships or races we’ve won in the past didn’t feel like this one." He continues: "It was a dream of mine, and seeing the whole team celebrate that is something I really have fresh in my memory. I want to do it again.”

driversAndNumbers.title: Julien Andlauer
driversAndNumbers.introduction: The talented Porsche works driver, Julien Andlauer, began his motorsport career in karting. He took part in various Porsche Carrera Cups, including in France and Germany. At the age of 18, Julien made motorsport history as the youngest class winner of the 24 Hours of Le Mans.
driversAndNumbers.introHeading: A new smiling face in the Porsche Penske family
driversAndNumbers.introColumn1: Andlauer had a stellar maiden Hypercar season 2024 in the WEC with the Porsche customer racing team Proton Competition. His season impressed fans, the Porsche Penske Motorsport team and also the WEC itself, which presented him with the Revelation of the Year award in Bahrain which he says was a “huge surprise.”
driversAndNumbers.introColumn2: He has been a works driver in the Porsche Penske Motorsport Team since 2025. Since 2026 he drives the #7 Porsche 963 alongside Felipe Nasr in the IMSA WeatherTec SportsCar Championship.
driversAndNumbers.seoMetaDescription: Discover the profile of Julien Andlauer, a rising star as Porsche factory driver. Explore his career highlights, achievements, and insights into his journey as a professional driver in the world of motorsport.

driversAndNumbers.title: Laurin Heinrich
driversAndNumbers.introduction: Laurin Heinrich began his Porsche journey in the Porsche Carrera Cup Germany in 2020. He quickly made his mark with strong performances in various GT championships over the years. In the 2025 IMSA season, he raced with the customer racing team AO Racing, and he will be supporting Porsche Penske Motorsport with the 963 in endurance races during the 2026 IMSA season as the third driver.
